object: A-frame step ladder: painted pressed-steel side rails, five flat stamped treads riveted between them, a hinged rear frame, rubber feet
understanding: The rails are thin folded channel; they kink and bend when the ladder is dropped or overloaded, more than they dent.
Treads are stamped sheet with ribs; they dish in when something heavy lands on them, and their front edges get dinged.
Hurt by falling over, being thrown in a van, overloading and being stood on wrong: bent rails, twisted frame, dinged tread edges.
Paint wears through on tread tops and front edges, rail edges and the feet; rust starts at the rivets, hinges and where the feet stand in water.
